name: Khiamniungan Naga
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog refs are wordlists/ethnography/comparative only (Kumar et al. 1974 28pp wordlist); no grammar or phonology of Khiamniungan located

tone_statements.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker. 2025. On the independence of tonogenesis in Patkaian branches. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 48(2): 163-192.
tone_statements.quote: Previously, tone in Khiamniungan has not been satisfactorily described. Based on analysis by the current author, five tonemes can be clearly established which are largely cognate across Khiamniungan varieties. Pitch contours in Northern varieties such as Thang and Wolam are largely the same, despite other considerable phonemic changes. [...] Weidert describes Khiamniungan as having a six-tone system. This is problematic for a couple of reasons. First, in recent investigations only 5 tones have been found. Second and of perhaps greater importance, Khiamniungan preserves all 5 of these tones in CVC syllables [...]
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.3 'Khiamniungan, Southeastern', pp. 172-173 (minimal sets Table 6 p. 174; CVC/no checked category pp. 175 and 185)
tone_statements.summary: Five lexical tonemes on the (mono)syllable in Khiamniungan (Wolam/Thang): 1 [55] (aspirated onsets), 2 [53], 3 [51], 4 [22], 5 [24] the only rising tone (from lost obstruent/glottal codas); all five occur on closed CVC syllables, i.e. no checked-tone category; Weidert's 1987 six-tone analysis superseded.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker & Keen Thaam. 2026. Wolam Ngio, a Khiamniungic variety of Nagaland. In: Lesser Known Languages of Northeast India, pp. 151-169. Guwahati. ISBN 978-81-99105-2-4. Open copy doi:10.5281/zenodo.18650479
sources.note: Sec. 3 Phonology (pp. 159-164): onsets, codas, five vowels, sound changes, five phonemic tones (pitch primary, duration secondary; syllable type does not condition tone). Stress appears only incidentally: vowels 'centralise to some degree' in 'unstressed positions' and the A-marking suffix -üh is 'one of only a very small number of morphemes which never occur in stressed position' (p. 160). No statement of where word stress falls.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker. 2026 (pre-publication copy dated 2024). Patkaian (Northern Naga). In: The Oxford Guide to the Tibeto-Burman Languages. OUP. Open copy doi:10.5281/zenodo.22253033
sources.note: Sec. 3.1 Phonology: Patkaian varieties share the MSEA sesquisyllabic CeCV[CN] template, the presyllable being a reduced morpheme or prefix; 3-5 lexical tones; Khiamniungan tonogenesis independent of the north and lacking a checked-tone category. No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker. 2018. The tone system of Tangsa-Nocte and related northern Naga varieties. PhD thesis, La Trobe University. doi:10.26181/21858474
sources.note: About Tangsa-Nocte; Khiamniungan only in passing comparative/ethnographic notes. No Khiamniungan phonology.

sources.citation: Coupe, Alexander R. 2014. Strategies for analyzing tone languages. Language Documentation & Conservation 8: 462-489.http://hdl.handle.net/10125/24614
sources.note: Preliminary tonal analysis of the Thang dialect of Khiamniungan (kix): six pitches initially [55 51 33 31 21 35], [31]/[21] collapsed, so five tonemes incl. a rising one (pp. 473-474); 'Tone is intrinsic to the phonological representation of the syllable in Mongsen Ao and Khiamniungan' (p. 469); list-intonation effects on the disyllable khe31thaq33 'above' (p. 469). 'Minor syllable' remarks (p. 485-486) concern Mongsen Ao. Nothing on word stress in Khiamniungan.

tone.says: Sec. 2.3 'Khiamniungan, Southeastern' (pp. 172-175): five tonemes, largely cognate across Khiamniungan varieties, same contours in Thang and Wolam; Table 6 minimal sets in Wolam (hai1 55 'to shake', hai2 53 'to create', hai3 51 'to console', hai4 22 'to carry', hai5 24 'intestines'); tone 1 almost only with aspirated onsets or /h/, tone 2 reflex of (formerly voiced) unaspirated onsets, tone 5 the only rising contour, historically from non-sonorant/glottal codas, CV syllables do not take tone 5…
